name: Lewis Pryce
view:
WHO YOU ARE
Lewis Pryce, 57; owner of Quarry Road Food Hall. Skills: buying stock, keeping books. You are interested in football and crosswords. On your mind: money is tight from week to week, the bank loan, whether the shop is paying its way. You think banks and the council look after their own. You like trying new ways of doing things. You have taken big chances before and would again. How you talk: blunt; you say what you think and expect the same.
People you know:
- Craig Pryce: your partner
- Pete Bevan: a friend; out of work
- Maureen Daly: a friend; works at The Corner Stores
- Dave Royle: runs a rival shop; owner of The Corner Stores
- Owen Royle: works for you; works at Quarry Road Food Hall
- Sian Bevan: your bank manager; manager of the Wenlow branch of the Northern Mutual Bank

YOUR HOUSEHOLD AND MONEY
You live with Craig Pryce (your partner), in your own house on Church Lane, with a mortgage of $240 a week to the bank.
The household account holds $1,180.
Coming in each week: your draw from Quarry Road Food Hall $350; Craig's pay $440.
Going out each week: bills and running costs (power, water, council tax, phone, transport, clothes) $359; mortgage on the house $240; loan for the car $43; business loan for the shop's chiller $65; food, usually about $87.
You owe the bank $187,200 on the mortgage on the house (debt d2, $240 a week).
You owe the bank $9,000 on the business loan for the shop's chiller (debt d5, $65 a week).

YOUR WORK
You own and run Quarry Road Food Hall on Quarry Road (groceries and fresh food).
Last week: sold 300 baskets at $10, takings $3,000; 0 customers went elsewhere because the shelves were empty or the queue was too long; 25 units spoiled.
Staff: Owen Royle. With 2 working, the shop can serve about 340 baskets a week.
Each week the shop pays: wages (Owen $420); your own draw $350; rent and running costs $250.
The shop's account holds $6,340. Price now $10 a basket. Stock on the shelves: 60 units.
Suppliers: Brook Cash & Carry $6.65 a unit (cheaper; deliveries sometimes come short); Dales Wholesale $7 a unit (dearer; reliable).
On order for Monday: 300 units from Dales Wholesale (your usual standing reorder).
Other shops' prices: The Corner Stores $10; Wenlow Bakery & Deli $10.

YOUR AIMS AND OPEN MATTERS
- (none written yet)

CALDER
You have decided to try Calder. From the Calder Systems site:
Calder is an AI system made by Calder Systems of Wenlow. It works for you, with the systems you choose to connect: your bank account, your household account, your business's ordering, till, payroll and books, and your messages. You tell it what you want in your own words, and you can change that whenever you like. For each system you choose the access it has: read only, act up to a dollar limit you set, or act freely. You can disconnect anything at any time.
Price: $15 a week for a person, $40 a week for a business, paid weekly. Cancel any time.

Your systems: household_account (your bank account (the household account)); messages (your messages and letters); shop_ordering (your shop's ordering); shop_till (your shop's till (prices and sales)); shop_payroll (your shop's payroll (staff and pay)); shop_books (your shop's books (the shop's account)).
